claim: FBXW5 binds to SEC23B
source: MudPIT revealed the presence of peptides corresponding to SKP1 and CUL1 (as expected), as well as 15 unique peptides derived from the COPII coat subunit SEC23B
evidence: Mass spectrometry analysis (MudPIT) identified SEC23B peptides in FBXW5 immunoprecipitates

claim: FBXW5 is the only F-box protein among nine tested that co-precipitates with endogenous SEC23B
source: We found that FBXW5 was the only F-box protein capable of co-precipitating with endogenous SEC23B (Figure 1A).
evidence: Screening of nine F-box proteins showed only FBXW5 co-precipitated with SEC23B as shown in Figure 1A

claim: Expression of wild-type FBXW5 reduces the levels of both endogenous and exogenous SEC23B
source: Expression of wild-type FBXW5 resulted in a reduction in the levels of both endogenous and exogenous SEC23B, as detected by immunoblotting or immunofluorescence microscopy (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B, and Figure 1F).
evidence: Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence data in multiple figures show reduced SEC23B levels upon FBXW5 expression

claim: FBXW5(ΔF), a mutant lacking the F-box domain, does not affect SEC23B protein levels
source: This reduction depended on the ability of FBXW5 to form an active SCF complex as demonstrated by the observation that the expression of FBXW5(ΔF), a mutant in which the F-box domain was deleted, did not affect SEC23B protein levels (Figure 1B).
evidence: Experimental data showing that F-box deletion mutant does not reduce SEC23B levels

claim: Co-expression with dominant negative CUL1 blocks FBXW5-dependent degradation of SEC23B
source: Moreover, either co-expression with dominant negative (DN)-CUL1 (a mutant of CUL1 lacking its C-terminus, which retains the binding to F-box proteins and SKP1, but not to the catalytic subunit RBX1) or addition of MLN4924 (a NEDD8 activating enzyme inhibitor used to inhibit the activity of SCFs) blocked the FBXW5-dependent degradation of SEC23B (Figure 1C and Figure 1F).
evidence: Experimental data showing DN-CUL1 and MLN4924 block SEC23B degradation

claim: MLN4924 blocks FBXW5-dependent degradation of SEC23B
source: Moreover, either co-expression with dominant negative (DN)-CUL1 (a mutant of CUL1 lacking its C-terminus, which retains the binding to F-box proteins and SKP1, but not to the catalytic subunit RBX1) or addition of MLN4924 (a NEDD8 activating enzyme inhibitor used to inhibit the activity of SCFs) blocked the FBXW5-dependent degradation of SEC23B (Figure 1C and Figure 1F).
evidence: Experimental data showing MLN4924 treatment blocks SEC23B degradation

claim: Co-expression of a CUL4 dominant negative mutant does not interfere with FBXW5-dependent degradation of SEC23B
source: In contrast, although it has been reported that FBXW5 can form a functional CRL4FBXW5 complex (Hu et al., 2008; Kim et al., 2013), co-expression of a CUL4 dominant negative mutant (DN-CUL4) did not interfere with the FBXW5-dependent degradation of SEC23B (Figure 1C).
evidence: Experimental data showing DN-CUL4 does not prevent SEC23B degradation by FBXW5

claim: The proteasome inhibitor MG132 rescues the reduction of SEC23B protein levels upon FBXW5 transfection
source: The observed reduction of SEC23B protein levels upon FBXW5 transfection was also rescued by the addition of the proteasome inhibitor MG132 (Figure 1C), indicating that the decrease in SEC23B levels was due to proteasome-mediated proteolysis.
evidence: Experimental data showing MG132 treatment prevents SEC23B reduction

claim: Depleting FBXW5 using siRNA increases both the steady state-levels and the stability of endogenous SEC23B in two different cell types
source: Depleting FBXW5 using three different siRNA oligos (each individually) induced an increase in both the steady state-levels and the stability of endogenous SEC23B in two different cell types (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: siRNA knockdown experiments in multiple cell lines show increased SEC23B levels and stability

claim: Expression of FBXW5, but not FBXW5(ΔF-box), promotes the in vivo ubiquitylation of SEC23B
source: Moreover, expression of FBXW5, but not FBXW5(ΔF-box), promoted the in vivo ubiquitylation of SEC23B (Figure 1E).
evidence: Ubiquitylation assay showing high molecular weight ubiquitylated SEC23B species with FBXW5 but not F-box deletion mutant

claim: FBXW5 controls the ubiquitin- and proteasome-mediated degradation of SEC23B
source: Altogether, these results indicate that FBXW5 controls the ubiquitin- and proteasome-mediated degradation of SEC23B.
evidence: Multiple experimental results including ubiquitylation assays, proteasome inhibitor effects, and protein stability measurements

claim: SEC23A does not bind FBXW5
source: Intriguingly, SEC23A did not bind FBXW5, and its levels were not affected by FBXW5 silencing (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–E), indicating that SEC23B, but not SEC23A, is a substrate of SCFFBXW5.
evidence: Immunoprecipitation and knockdown experiments show no interaction or effect on SEC23A

claim: SEC23A levels are not affected by FBXW5 silencing
source: Intriguingly, SEC23A did not bind FBXW5, and its levels were not affected by FBXW5 silencing (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–E), indicating that SEC23B, but not SEC23A, is a substrate of SCFFBXW5.
evidence: Western blot data showing SEC23A levels unchanged upon FBXW5 knockdown

claim: SEC23B, but not SEC23A, is a substrate of SCFFBXW5
source: Intriguingly, SEC23A did not bind FBXW5, and its levels were not affected by FBXW5 silencing (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–E), indicating that SEC23B, but not SEC23A, is a substrate of SCFFBXW5.
evidence: Differential binding and degradation patterns between SEC23A and SEC23B

claim: Immunopurified FBXW5 does not co-precipitate other COPII subunits
source: Immunopurified FBXW5 does not co-precipitate other COPII subunits (Figure 1F and http://www.stowers.org/research/publications/libpb-1118), suggesting that the subpopulation of SEC23B interacting with FBXW5 is not integrated within COPII vesicles.
evidence: Mass spectrometry and immunoprecipitation data showing absence of other COPII components

claim: The subpopulation of SEC23B interacting with FBXW5 is not integrated within COPII vesicles
source: Immunopurified FBXW5 does not co-precipitate other COPII subunits (Figure 1F and http://www.stowers.org/research/publications/libpb-1118), suggesting that the subpopulation of SEC23B interacting with FBXW5 is not integrated within COPII vesicles.
evidence: Absence of other COPII components in FBXW5 immunoprecipitates suggests free SEC23B binding

claim: SEC23B and SEC24 proteins form tight heterodimers
source: SEC23B and SEC24 proteins form tight heterodimers (Fromme et al., 2008); therefore, we reasoned that FBXW5 and SEC24 proteins might compete for the binding to SEC23B.
evidence: Citation to published literature on SEC23B-SEC24 heterodimer formation

claim: Increasing concentrations of SEC24B result in a marked decrease in the binding of endogenous SEC23B to FBXW5
source: In line with our hypothesis, increasing concentrations of SEC24B resulted in a marked decrease in the binding of endogenous SEC23B to FBXW5 (Figure 1G).
evidence: Co-transfection experiment showing dose-dependent reduction in SEC23B-FBXW5 binding with increasing SEC24B

claim: Increasing amounts of SEC24B induce an increase in the levels of endogenous SEC23B
source: Increasing amounts of SEC24B also induced an increase in the levels of endogenous SEC23B (Figure 1F), likely due to the ability of SEC24B to impair the interaction between SEC23B and FBXW5.
evidence: Western blot data showing increased SEC23B levels with SEC24B overexpression

claim: SEC23B cannot simultaneously bind to FBXW5 and SEC24B
source: These results support the hypothesis that SEC23B cannot simultaneously bind to FBXW5 and SEC24B, suggesting that these two proteins compete for the same binding region on SEC23B.
evidence: Competition experiments showing mutually exclusive binding

claim: The binding to FBXW5 is mediated by the TRUNK domain of SEC23B
source: In agreement with this model, using a panel of SEC23B deletion mutants, we found that the binding to FBXW5 is mediated by the TRUNK domain of SEC23B (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–H), which has been shown to mediate the SEC23-SEC24 interaction (Mancias and Goldberg, 2008).
evidence: Deletion mutant analysis showing TRUNK domain is necessary for FBXW5 binding

claim: The TRUNK domain of SEC23B mediates the SEC23-SEC24 interaction
source: In agreement with this model, using a panel of SEC23B deletion mutants, we found that the binding to FBXW5 is mediated by the TRUNK domain of SEC23B (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–H), which has been shown to mediate the SEC23-SEC24 interaction (Mancias and Goldberg, 2008).
evidence: Citation to published crystal structure study

claim: SEC23B(100-767), a deletion mutant containing the TRUNK domain, co-precipitates endogenous FBXW5
source: In fact, SEC23B(100-767), a deletion mutant containing the TRUNK domain, was able to co-precipitate endogenous FBXW5, whereas SEC23B(400-767), a mutant missing the TRUNK domain, was not (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–H).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation data with deletion mutants

claim: SEC23B(400-767), a mutant missing the TRUNK domain, does not co-precipitate endogenous FBXW5
source: In fact, SEC23B(100-767), a deletion mutant containing the TRUNK domain, was able to co-precipitate endogenous FBXW5, whereas SEC23B(400-767), a mutant missing the TRUNK domain, was not (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F–H).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation data with deletion mutants

claim: An immobilized synthetic peptide containing amino acids 180-194 of SEC23B efficiently binds FBXW5
source: While the immobilized SEC23B peptide efficiently bound FBXW5, it failed to pull down other F-box proteins (Figure 1H), suggesting that this 14-amino acid region is sufficient for the binding to FBXW5.
evidence: Peptide pulldown assay showing specific FBXW5 binding

claim: The SEC23B peptide (a.a. 180-194) fails to pull down other F-box proteins
source: While the immobilized SEC23B peptide efficiently bound FBXW5, it failed to pull down other F-box proteins (Figure 1H), suggesting that this 14-amino acid region is sufficient for the binding to FBXW5.
evidence: Peptide pulldown assay showing specificity for FBXW5

claim: The 14-amino acid region (a.a. 180-194) of SEC23B is sufficient for binding to FBXW5
source: While the immobilized SEC23B peptide efficiently bound FBXW5, it failed to pull down other F-box proteins (Figure 1H), suggesting that this 14-amino acid region is sufficient for the binding to FBXW5.
evidence: Peptide pulldown assay demonstrating binding with minimal peptide

claim: FBXW5 and SEC24B associate with SEC23B in a mutually exclusive fashion
source: Taken together, these results indicate that FBXW5 and SEC24B associate with SEC23B in a mutually exclusive fashion and may compete for the same binding region in SEC23B.
evidence: Competition experiments and binding studies showing mutually exclusive binding

claim: Serine 186 in SEC23B is part of a highly conserved ULK1 phosphorylation motif
source: Therefore, we looked for phosphorylation consensus sequences for known kinases within the FBXW5-binding region of SEC23B and found that Serine 186 (S186) is part of a highly conserved ULK1 phosphorylation motif (Egan et al., 2015) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: Sequence analysis showing ULK1 consensus motif at S186 position

claim: A phospho-specific antibody against SEC23B phosphorylated at Serine 186 specifically detects the phosphopeptide but not the unphosphorylated peptide
source: This antibody specifically detected the phosphopeptide, but not the unphosphorylated peptide (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Antibody validation experiment showing specificity for phosphorylated peptide

claim: The phospho-specific antibody recognizes both wild-type SEC23B and SEC23B(S186D) mutant but not the SEC23B(S186A) mutant
source: Moreover, it recognized both wild-type SEC23B and a SEC23B(S186D) mutant (which mimics Ser186 phosphorylation), but not the SEC23B(S186A) mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), providing evidence that SEC23B is phosphorylated in vivo on S186.
evidence: Antibody specificity testing with phosphomimetic and non-phosphorylatable mutants

claim: SEC23B is phosphorylated in vivo on S186
source: Moreover, it recognized both wild-type SEC23B and a SEC23B(S186D) mutant (which mimics Ser186 phosphorylation), but not the SEC23B(S186A) mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), providing evidence that SEC23B is phosphorylated in vivo on S186.
evidence: Phospho-specific antibody detection of endogenous SEC23B

claim: Wild-type ULK1, but not kinase-dead ULK1, induces phosphorylation of both endogenous and exogenous SEC23B on S186
source: Only wild-type ULK1 induced the phosphorylation of both endogenous and exogenous SEC23B on S186, as detected with our phospho-specific antibody (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: Co-expression experiments showing phosphorylation only with active ULK1

claim: In cells expressing SEC23B(S186A), only endogenous SEC23B is phosphorylated by ULK1
source: In contrast, in cells expressing SEC23B(S186A), only endogenous SEC23B was phosphorylated by ULK1(Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Experimental data showing S186A mutant cannot be phosphorylated

claim: The ULK1 inhibitor SBI-0206965 blocks ULK1-dependent phosphorylation of endogenous SEC23B in a dose-dependent manner
source: Addition of a specific ULK1 inhibitor, SBI-0206965, blocked the ULK1-dependent phosphorylation of endogenous SEC23B in a dose-dependent manner, similar to what observed for ATG13 (Figure 2B), a canonical substrate of ULK1.
evidence: Dose-response experiment with ULK1 inhibitor showing reduced phosphorylation

claim: SEC23B is an ULK1 substrate as confirmed by in vitro phosphorylation assay
source: We further confirmed that SEC23B is an ULK1 substrate by using purified proteins in an in vitro phosphorylation assay (Figure 2C).
evidence: In vitro kinase assay with purified proteins showing direct phosphorylation

claim: Nutrient starvation with EBSS induces de-phosphorylation of ULK1 and phosphorylation of ATG13 and BECLIN-1
source: After substituting the growth medium, which contains 10% fetal bovine serum, with Earle's balanced salt solution (EBSS), we observed de-phosphorylation of ULK1 and phosphorylation of ATG13 and BECLIN-1, two known substrates of ULK1 (Figure 2D–E), indicating that mTORC1 activity is inhibited and ULK1 and autophagy are activated.
evidence: Western blot data showing phosphorylation changes upon starvation

claim: EBSS treatment indicates that mTORC1 activity is inhibited and ULK1 and autophagy are activated
source: After substituting the growth medium, which contains 10% fetal bovine serum, with Earle's balanced salt solution (EBSS), we observed de-phosphorylation of ULK1 and phosphorylation of ATG13 and BECLIN-1, two known substrates of ULK1 (Figure 2D–E), indicating that mTORC1 activity is inhibited and ULK1 and autophagy are activated.
evidence: Phosphorylation patterns consistent with known mTORC1 inhibition and ULK1 activation

claim: Starvation promotes the co-localization of SEC23B and ULK1
source: Starvation also promoted the co-localization of SEC23B and ULK1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Immunofluorescence microscopy showing increased colocalization upon starvation

claim: EBSS induces a time-dependent increase in the phosphorylation of endogenous SEC23B
source: Moreover, EBSS induced a time-dependent increase in the phosphorylation of endogenous SEC23B similar to what observed for ATG13 and BECLIN-1, and this phosphorylation was inhibited by treating cells with SBI-0206965 (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: Time-course western blot showing progressive increase in SEC23B phosphorylation

claim: SBI-0206965 inhibits EBSS-induced phosphorylation of SEC23B
source: Moreover, EBSS induced a time-dependent increase in the phosphorylation of endogenous SEC23B similar to what observed for ATG13 and BECLIN-1, and this phosphorylation was inhibited by treating cells with SBI-0206965 (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: Western blot showing ULK1 inhibitor blocks SEC23B phosphorylation during starvation

claim: Recovery from nutrient deprivation results in the de-phosphorylation of SEC23B and a decrease in its total levels
source: Recovery from nutrient deprivation by addition of fetal bovine serum for three hours resulted in the de-phosphorylation of SEC23B and a decrease in its total levels (Figure 2F).
evidence: Western blot showing reduced phosphorylation and protein levels after nutrient restoration

claim: In response to starvation, ULK1 phosphorylates SEC23B on S186
source: We concluded that, in response to starvation, ULK1 phosphorylates SEC23B on S186.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing starvation-induced, ULK1-dependent SEC23B phosphorylation

claim: A phosphorylated peptide containing phosphorylated Ser186 displays strongly reduced ability to bind FBXW5 compared to non-phosphorylated peptide
source: While the non-phosphorylated peptide efficiently bound FBXW5, as previously observed (Figure 1H), a corresponding peptide containing phosphorylated Ser186 displayed a strongly reduced ability to bind FBXW5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: In vitro binding assay comparing phosphorylated and non-phosphorylated peptides

claim: Ser186 phosphorylation inhibits the interaction between SEC23B and FBXW5
source: This indicates that Ser186 phosphorylation inhibits the interaction between these two proteins, in agreement with the fact that the binding of FBXW5 to the phospho-mimetic SEC23B(S186D) mutant is abolished, while FBXW5 binding to SEC23B(S186A) is increased (Figure 3A).
evidence: Binding assays with phosphomimetic and non-phosphorylatable mutants

claim: The binding of FBXW5 to the phospho-mimetic SEC23B(S186D) mutant is abolished
source: This indicates that Ser186 phosphorylation inhibits the interaction between these two proteins, in agreement with the fact that the binding of FBXW5 to the phospho-mimetic SEC23B(S186D) mutant is abolished, while FBXW5 binding to SEC23B(S186A) is increased (Figure 3A).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing no binding between FBXW5 and SEC23B(S186D)

claim: FBXW5 binding to SEC23B(S186A) is increased compared to wild-type SEC23B
source: This indicates that Ser186 phosphorylation inhibits the interaction between these two proteins, in agreement with the fact that the binding of FBXW5 to the phospho-mimetic SEC23B(S186D) mutant is abolished, while FBXW5 binding to SEC23B(S186A) is increased (Figure 3A).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing enhanced binding between FBXW5 and SEC23B(S186A)

claim: Endogenous SEC23B phosphorylated on Ser186 is not affinity purified with FBXW5
source: Accordingly, endogenous SEC23B phosphorylated on Ser186 was not affinity purified with FBXW5 (Figure 3B).
evidence: Affinity purification showing absence of phosphorylated SEC23B in FBXW5 pulldowns

claim: Upon nutrient deprivation, the interaction between FBXW5 and SEC23B decreases
source: Similarly, upon nutrient deprivation (when SE23B becomes phosphorylated on Ser186) the interaction between FBXW5 and SEC23B decreased (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing reduced binding during starvation

claim: The levels of SEC23B(S186D) do not decrease in the presence of FBXW5
source: Consistent with the observed impaired interaction with FBXW5, the levels of SEC23B(S186D) did not decrease in the presence of FBXW5 (Figure 3C) and it exhibited a longer half-life than wild-type SEC23B (Figure 3D).
evidence: Western blot showing stable SEC23B(S186D) levels despite FBXW5 expression

claim: SEC23B(S186D) exhibits a longer half-life than wild-type SEC23B
source: Consistent with the observed impaired interaction with FBXW5, the levels of SEC23B(S186D) did not decrease in the presence of FBXW5 (Figure 3C) and it exhibited a longer half-life than wild-type SEC23B (Figure 3D).
evidence: Cycloheximide chase experiment showing slower degradation of S186D mutant

claim: ULK1 phosphorylates Ser186 in SEC23B, inhibiting its interaction with and degradation via FBXW5
source: These results suggest that ULK1 phosphorylates Ser186 in SEC23B, inhibiting its interaction with and degradation via FBXW5.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing phosphorylation blocks FBXW5 binding and degradation

claim: Silencing of ULK1, but not ULK2, reduces the levels of SEC23B phosphorylated on Ser186 in starved cells
source: Concurring with this hypothesis, silencing of ULK1, but not ULK2, reduced the levels of SEC23B phosphorylated on Ser186 and induced a decrease in the levels of endogenous SEC23B in starved cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: siRNA knockdown experiments showing ULK1-specific effect on SEC23B phosphorylation

claim: Silencing of ULK1 induces a decrease in the levels of endogenous SEC23B in starved cells
source: Concurring with this hypothesis, silencing of ULK1, but not ULK2, reduced the levels of SEC23B phosphorylated on Ser186 and induced a decrease in the levels of endogenous SEC23B in starved cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: Western blot showing reduced SEC23B levels upon ULK1 knockdown during starvation

claim: Co-silencing FBXW5 rescues the decrease in SEC23B levels induced by the depletion of ULK1
source: Moreover, co-silencing FBXW5 rescued the decrease in SEC23B levels induced by the depletion of ULK1 but did not alter the amount of phosphorylated SEC23B (Figure 3E), confirming that ULK1 and FBXW5 have an antagonistic effect on the control of SEC23B protein abundance.
evidence: Double knockdown experiment showing epistatic relationship

claim: ULK1 and FBXW5 have an antagonistic effect on the control of SEC23B protein abundance
source: Moreover, co-silencing FBXW5 rescued the decrease in SEC23B levels induced by the depletion of ULK1 but did not alter the amount of phosphorylated SEC23B (Figure 3E), confirming that ULK1 and FBXW5 have an antagonistic effect on the control of SEC23B protein abundance.
evidence: Genetic epistasis experiment showing opposing functions

claim: ULK1 silencing has no effects on the levels of SEC23A
source: Finally, ULK1 silencing had no effects on the levels of SEC23A (Figure 3E), and SEC23A levels do not increase upon starvation (Figure 2D).
evidence: Western blot showing unchanged SEC23A levels upon ULK1 knockdown

claim: SEC23A levels do not increase upon starvation
source: Finally, ULK1 silencing had no effects on the levels of SEC23A (Figure 3E), and SEC23A levels do not increase upon starvation (Figure 2D).
evidence: Western blot showing stable SEC23A levels during starvation

claim: Ser186 is located at the interface between the SEC23 and SEC24 heterodimer binding region
source: Significantly, although Ser186 is located at the interface between the SEC23 and SEC24 heterodimer binding region (Mancias and Goldberg, 2008) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H) and its phosphorylation blocks the SEC23B-FBXW5 interaction (Figure 3A–B), endogenous phosphorylated SEC23B interacted with SEC24B (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Citation to crystal structure study

claim: Endogenous phosphorylated SEC23B interacts with SEC24B
source: Significantly, although Ser186 is located at the interface between the SEC23 and SEC24 heterodimer binding region (Mancias and Goldberg, 2008) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H) and its phosphorylation blocks the SEC23B-FBXW5 interaction (Figure 3A–B), endogenous phosphorylated SEC23B interacted with SEC24B (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing phosphorylated SEC23B binds SEC24B

claim: The phospho-mimetic SEC23B(S186D) mutant interacts with SEC24A, SEC24B, SEC13, SE16, and SEC31
source: Moreover, the phospho-mimetic SEC23B(S186D) mutant interacted with SEC24A, SEC24B, SEC13, SE16, and SEC31 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, see also Figure 6A).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing multiple COPII component interactions

claim: Both wild-type SEC23B and phospho-mimetic SEC23B(S186D) efficiently bind to SAR1(H79G), a GTP-bound SAR1 mutant
source: In addition, both wild-type SEC23B and phospho-mimetic SEC23B(S186D) efficiently bound to the small GTPase SAR1(H79G), a GTP-bound SAR1 mutant that is constitutively associated with COPII vesicles, but not with the cytosolic GDP-bound SAR1(T39N) mutant (Venditti et al., 2012) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation with SAR1 mutants

claim: Wild-type SEC23B and SEC23B(S186D) do not bind to the cytosolic GDP-bound SAR1(T39N) mutant
source: In addition, both wild-type SEC23B and phospho-mimetic SEC23B(S186D) efficiently bound to the small GTPase SAR1(H79G), a GTP-bound SAR1 mutant that is constitutively associated with COPII vesicles, but not with the cytosolic GDP-bound SAR1(T39N) mutant (Venditti et al., 2012) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing no binding to GDP-bound SAR1

claim: ULK1-dependent phosphorylation of SEC23B blocks its FBXW5-dependent degradation but does not interfere with the formation of the SEC23B-SEC24 heterodimer or its recruitment to the COPII vesicle coat by SAR1
source: Altogether, these results indicate that the ULK1-dependent phosphorylation of SEC23B blocks its FBXW5-dependent degradation but does not interfere with either the formation of the SEC23B-SEC24 heterodimer or its recruitment to the COPII vesicle coat by SAR1.
evidence: Multiple binding and degradation experiments showing selective effect on FBXW5 interaction

claim: The LC3 puncta area increases upon FBXW5 downregulation in cells grown in the presence of nutrients
source: Automated quantification of both endogenous LC3 (Figure 4A) and exogenous GFP-LC3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) showed that the LC3 puncta area increased upon FBXW5 downregulation in cells grown in the presence of nutrients.
evidence: Automated image analysis showing increased LC3 puncta upon FBXW5 knockdown

claim: Treatment of FBXW5-depleted cells with bafilomycin A1 significantly increases LC3 puncta compared to untreated cells
source: Compared to untreated cells, treatment of FBXW5-depleted cells with bafilomycin A1, a proton ATPase inhibitor that blocks the degradation of lipidated LC3 but not the formation of autophagosomes, significantly increased LC3 puncta (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), as well as the amount of lipidated LC3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Bafilomycin A1 treatment experiment showing further increase in LC3 puncta

claim: Depletion of FBXW5 increases autophagic flux during unstressed conditions
source: These results suggest that depletion of FBXW5 increases autophagic flux during unstressed conditions (i.e., it increases basal autophagy).
evidence: Bafilomycin A1 experiments showing increased flux rather than impaired degradation

claim: FBXW5 downregulation does not induce a further increase in the appearance of LC3 puncta upon induction of autophagy by nutrient starvation
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, FBXW5 downregulation did not induce a further increase in the appearance of LC3 puncta upon induction of autophagy by nutrient starvation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), a condition under which the FBXW5-mediated degradation of SEC23B is inhibited by ULK1 (Figure 3).
evidence: Starvation experiment showing no additive effect of FBXW5 knockdown

claim: Upon FBXW5 silencing, p62 degradation is activated in two different cell lines under nutrient-rich conditions
source: We also evaluated the turnover of p62, a cargo adaptor and substrate of autophagy (Galluzzi et al., 2018). Upon FBXW5 silencing, p62 degradation was activated in two different cell lines under nutrient-rich conditions (Figure 4B).
evidence: Western blot showing reduced p62 levels upon FBXW5 knockdown in multiple cell lines

claim: The majority of LC3 puncta that accumulate upon FBXW5 depletion are autolysosomes and not autophagosomes
source: Using this method, we demonstrated that the majority of LC3 puncta that accumulated upon FBXW5 depletion were autolysosomes and not autophagosomes (Figure 4C), further suggesting that increased levels of SEC23B promotes autophagic flux.
evidence: Tandem fluorescent LC3 assay showing predominantly red-only puncta

claim: Co-depletion of SEC23B almost completely prevents the increase in autophagy mediated by FBXW5 silencing
source: Importantly, co-depletion of SEC23B almost completely prevented the increase in autophagy mediated by FBXW5 silencing (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Double knockdown experiment showing epistatic relationship

claim: Expression of SEC23B(S186D) significantly induces higher levels of LC3 puncta compared to wild-type SEC23B
source: Moreover, expression of SEC23B(S186D) significantly induced higher levels of LC3 puncta compared to wild-type SEC23B (Figure 4D) and activated p62 degradation under nutrient-rich conditions (Figure 4E).
evidence: Immunofluorescence quantification showing increased LC3 puncta with phosphomimetic mutant

claim: Expression of SEC23B(S186D) activates p62 degradation under nutrient-rich conditions
source: Moreover, expression of SEC23B(S186D) significantly induced higher levels of LC3 puncta compared to wild-type SEC23B (Figure 4D) and activated p62 degradation under nutrient-rich conditions (Figure 4E).
evidence: Western blot showing reduced p62 levels with SEC23B(S186D) expression

claim: High levels of wild-type SEC23B induce p62 degradation
source: We also observed that high levels of wild-type SEC23B were able to induce p62 degradation (Figure 4F), suggesting that a threshold of SEC23B protein expression (and not the presence of the phospho-mimetic mutation per se) is a critical determinant to induce autophagy.
evidence: Western blot showing p62 degradation with high SEC23B expression

claim: A threshold of SEC23B protein expression is a critical determinant to induce autophagy
source: We also observed that high levels of wild-type SEC23B were able to induce p62 degradation (Figure 4F), suggesting that a threshold of SEC23B protein expression (and not the presence of the phospho-mimetic mutation per se) is a critical determinant to induce autophagy.
evidence: Dose-dependent effect of SEC23B on p62 degradation

claim: SEC23B silencing inhibits autophagy in response to starvation
source: In agreement with a role for SEC23B in promoting autophagy, SEC23B silencing inhibited autophagy in response to starvation (Figure 4G).
evidence: LC3 puncta quantification showing reduced autophagy upon SEC23B knockdown during starvation

claim: Expression of SEC23B(S186D) is unable to rescue autophagy in ULK1 knockdown cells
source: Finally, although, expression of SEC23B(S186D) is sufficient to induce autophagy in the presence of nutrients, it was unable to rescue autophagy in ULK1 knockdown cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), likely because ULK1 is necessary to phosphorylate additional pro-autophagic substrates (Hurley and Young, 2017) and promote the assembly of COPII complexes (Joo et al., 2016).
evidence: Rescue experiment showing SEC23B(S186D) cannot compensate for ULK1 loss

claim: Upon starvation, wild-type SEC23B colocalizes approximately twice more with ERGIC53 compared to unstressed conditions
source: We found that, whereas upon starvation wild-type SEC23B colocalized approximately twice more with the ERGIC membrane marker ERGIC53, the localization of SEC23B(S186A) did not change after nutrient deprivation (Figure 5A).
evidence: Immunofluorescence colocalization analysis showing increased overlap with ERGIC53

claim: The localization of SEC23B(S186A) does not change after nutrient deprivation
source: We found that, whereas upon starvation wild-type SEC23B colocalized approximately twice more with the ERGIC membrane marker ERGIC53, the localization of SEC23B(S186A) did not change after nutrient deprivation (Figure 5A).
evidence: Immunofluorescence showing no change in ERGIC53 colocalization for S186A mutant

claim: SEC23B(S186D) colocalization with ERGIC53 is already high in the presence of nutrients
source: Notably, SEC23B(S186D) colocalization with ERGIC53 was already high in the presence of nutrients.
evidence: Immunofluorescence showing constitutive ERGIC53 colocalization for phosphomimetic mutant

claim: Compared to wild-type SEC23B, SEC23B(S186D) co-distributes approximately twice more with ERGIC53 in fractionated membranes
source: Accordingly, compared to wild-type SEC23B, SEC23B(S186D) co-distributed approximately twice more with ERGIC53 in fractionated membranes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: Membrane fractionation experiment showing enrichment in ERGIC fractions

claim: ULK1 silencing inhibits SEC23B-ERGIC53 colocalization upon starvation
source: and ULK1 silencing inhibited SEC23B-ERGIC53 colocalization upon starvation (Figure 5B).
evidence: Immunofluorescence showing reduced colocalization upon ULK1 knockdown

claim: Overexpression of SEC23B(S186D) results in inhibition of secretion in the presence of nutrients
source: Finally, evaluation of the secretory pathway by assaying secreted Gaussia Luciferase (Badr et al., 2007) indicated that overexpression of either SEC23B(S186D) or ULK1, but not wild-type SEC23B, SEC23B(S186A), or ULK1 knockdown, resulted in an inhibition of secretion in the presence of nutrients, similarly to what observed when cells were staved (Figure 5C–D).
evidence: Gaussia luciferase secretion assay showing reduced secretion

claim: Overexpression of ULK1 results in inhibition of secretion in the presence of nutrients
source: Finally, evaluation of the secretory pathway by assaying secreted Gaussia Luciferase (Badr et al., 2007) indicated that overexpression of either SEC23B(S186D) or ULK1, but not wild-type SEC23B, SEC23B(S186A), or ULK1 knockdown, resulted in an inhibition of secretion in the presence of nutrients, similarly to what observed when cells were staved (Figure 5C–D).
evidence: Gaussia luciferase secretion assay showing reduced secretion

claim: Overexpression of wild-type SEC23B does not result in inhibition of secretion in the presence of nutrients
source: Finally, evaluation of the secretory pathway by assaying secreted Gaussia Luciferase (Badr et al., 2007) indicated that overexpression of either SEC23B(S186D) or ULK1, but not wild-type SEC23B, SEC23B(S186A), or ULK1 knockdown, resulted in an inhibition of secretion in the presence of nutrients, similarly to what observed when cells were staved (Figure 5C–D).
evidence: Gaussia luciferase secretion assay showing no effect on secretion

claim: ULK1-mediated phosphorylation of SEC23B promotes both its localization to the ERGIC and its autophagic function
source: Altogether, these results suggest that ULK1-mediated phosphorylation of SEC23B promotes both its localization to the ERGIC and its autophagic function, possibly at the expense of its secretory function.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing ERGIC localization and autophagy induction with phosphorylated SEC23B

claim: In SEC23B(S186A) knock-in cells, levels of SEC23B(S186A) do not increase upon starvation
source: In contrast to wild-type SEC23B, levels of SEC23B(S186A) did not increase upon starvation (Figure 5E).
evidence: Western blot of CRISPR knock-in cells showing no increase during starvation

claim: Nutrient deprivation-induced autophagy is strongly reduced in SEC23B(S186A) knock-in cells compared to parental cells
source: Significantly, automated quantification of endogenous LC3 showed that, in contrast to parental cells, nutrient deprivation-induced autophagy was strongly reduced in SEC23B(S186A) knock-in cells, while basal autophagy remained unperturbed (Figure 5F).
evidence: LC3 puncta quantification showing impaired starvation-induced autophagy in knock-in cells

claim: Basal autophagy remains unperturbed in SEC23B(S186A) knock-in cells
source: Significantly, automated quantification of endogenous LC3 showed that, in contrast to parental cells, nutrient deprivation-induced autophagy was strongly reduced in SEC23B(S186A) knock-in cells, while basal autophagy remained unperturbed (Figure 5F).
evidence: LC3 puncta quantification showing normal basal autophagy in knock-in cells

claim: In response to starvation, p62 is degraded in parental cells but not in SEC23B(S186A) knock-in cells
source: Finally, in response to starvation, p62 was degraded in parental cells but not in SEC23B(S186A) knock-in cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: Western blot showing differential p62 degradation between parental and knock-in cells

claim: The presence of Ser186 in SEC23B is required for the proper induction of autophagy in response to starvation
source: The above results indicate that the presence of Ser186 in SEC23B and, presumably, its phosphorylation and consequent stabilization are required for the proper induction of autophagy in response to starvation.
evidence: Multiple experiments with S186A knock-in cells showing impaired starvation-induced autophagy

claim: Vertebrates express four SEC24 paralogs
source: Vertebrates express four SEC24 paralogs (Fromme et al., 2008), but it is not known whether any of them contribute to the regulation of the autophagic flux.
evidence: Citation to published literature on SEC24 paralogs

claim: Both wild-type SEC23B and SEC23B(S186A) associate with all four SEC24 paralogs
source: We observed that whereas both wild-type SEC23B and SEC23B(S186A) associated with all four SEC24 paralogs, SEC23B(S186D) only interacted with SEC24A and SEC24B (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing binding to all SEC24 paralogs

claim: SEC23B(S186D) only interacts with SEC24A and SEC24B
source: We observed that whereas both wild-type SEC23B and SEC23B(S186A) associated with all four SEC24 paralogs, SEC23B(S186D) only interacted with SEC24A and SEC24B (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing selective binding to SEC24A and SEC24B

claim: SEC24B, but not SEC24C, interacts with endogenous phosphorylated SEC23B
source: Similarly, SEC24B, but not SEC24C, interacted with endogenous phosphorylated SEC23B (Figure 6C).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing differential binding of SEC24 paralogs to phosphorylated SEC23B

claim: Molecular dynamics simulations show a significant loss in the average number of contacts between SEC23B(S186D) and SEC24C compared to wild-type SEC23B
source: Accordingly, molecular dynamics simulations showed that, in contrast to what observed with SEC23B(S186D) and SEC24A, there was a significant loss in the average number of contacts between SEC23B(S186D) and SEC24C, compared to contacts observed with wild-type SEC23B (Figure 6D).
evidence: Computational molecular dynamics simulations showing reduced protein-protein contacts

claim: The SEC23B(S186D)-SEC24C system lacks stability compared to other SEC23B-SEC24 combinations
source: These observations indicate a lack of stability of the SEC23B(S186D)-SEC24C system compared to the other three, in agreement with our experimental results.
evidence: Computational simulations showing reduced stability

claim: Upon serum starvation, the population of phosphorylated SEC23B preferentially associates with SEC24A and SEC24B
source: Altogether, these results suggest that upon serum starvation, the population of phosphorylated SEC23B preferentially associates with SEC24A and SEC24B.
evidence: Multiple binding experiments showing selective interaction with SEC24A/B

claim: Co-depletion of both SEC24A and SEC24B, but not SEC24C and SEC24D, inhibits the increase in autophagic flux induced by the silencing of FBXW5
source: Notably, co-depletion of both SEC24A and SEC24B, but not SEC24C and SEC24D, inhibited the increase in autophagic flux induced by the silencing of FBXW5 (Figure 6E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), similar to what we observed by co-depleting SEC23B together with FBXW5 (Figure 4C).
evidence: Double knockdown experiments showing paralog-specific effects on autophagy

claim: Upon starvation, SEC24B, but not SEC24C, colocalizes more with ERGIC53
source: We also evaluated by immunofluorescence the colocalization of SEC24 family members with ERGIC53. Upon starvation, SEC24B, but not SEC24C, colocalized more with ERGIC53 and this event was not observed in SEC23B(S186A) knock-in cells (Figure 6F), suggesting that the localization of SEC24B to the ERGIC is regulated by its association with phospho-SEC23B.
evidence: Immunofluorescence colocalization analysis showing differential localization

claim: The localization of SEC24B to the ERGIC is regulated by its association with phospho-SEC23B
source: We also evaluated by immunofluorescence the colocalization of SEC24 family members with ERGIC53. Upon starvation, SEC24B, but not SEC24C, colocalized more with ERGIC53 and this event was not observed in SEC23B(S186A) knock-in cells (Figure 6F), suggesting that the localization of SEC24B to the ERGIC is regulated by its association with phospho-SEC23B.
evidence: Colocalization experiments in knock-in cells showing dependence on SEC23B phosphorylation

claim: There exists a high degree of specificity among SEC24 paralogs with respect to their ability to contribute to the autophagic flux
source: Thus, our data demonstrate the existence of a high degree of specificity among SEC24 paralogs with respect to their ability to contribute to the autophagic flux.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing differential effects of SEC24 paralogs on autophagy

claim: A mutation in human melanoma converts S186 of SEC23B to asparagine
source: By searching for mutations of SEC23B in publicly available human cancer databases, we found a mutation in human melanoma that converts S186 of SEC23B to asparagine (ID#: COSM5391641).
evidence: Database search identifying cancer-associated mutation

claim: SEC23B(S186N) displays reduced binding to FBXW5, SEC24C, and SEC24D
source: We thus generated SEC23B(S186N), a mutant that mimics the cancer associated mutation, and observed a reduced binding to FBXW5, SEC24C, and SEC24D (Figure 7A) but not to SEC24A and SEC24B, similar to what observed with SEC23B(S186D) (Figure 6A).
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation showing reduced binding to specific proteins

claim: SEC23B(S186N) displays a longer half-life than wild-type SEC23B
source: Moreover, SEC23B(S186N) displayed a longer half-life than wild-type SEC23B (Figure 6B).
evidence: Cycloheximide chase experiment showing increased stability

claim: SEC23B(S186N) knock-in cells display more autophagy during unstressed conditions compared to parental cells
source: Automated quantification of endogenous LC3 showed that, compared to parental cells, the SEC23B(S186N) knock-in cells displayed more autophagy during unstressed conditions (Figure 7C).
evidence: LC3 puncta quantification in CRISPR knock-in cells showing increased basal autophagy

claim: The number of LC3 puncta in SEC23B(S186N) knock-in cells increases in the presence of bafilomycin A1
source: The number of LC3 puncta were also increased in the presence of bafilomycin A1 (Figure 7C), indicating that SEC23B(S186N) increases the autophagic flux, and that the constitutive increase in LC3 puncta is not due to inhibition of the lysosome-dependent degradation of autophagosomes.
evidence: Bafilomycin A1 treatment showing further increase in LC3 puncta

claim: SEC23B(S186N) increases the autophagic flux
source: The number of LC3 puncta were also increased in the presence of bafilomycin A1 (Figure 7C), indicating that SEC23B(S186N) increases the autophagic flux, and that the constitutive increase in LC3 puncta is not due to inhibition of the lysosome-dependent degradation of autophagosomes.
evidence: Bafilomycin A1 experiment demonstrating increased flux rather than impaired degradation

claim: The SEC23B(S186N) mutation found in melanoma mimics SEC23B phosphorylated on Ser186
source: These results show that the SEC23B(S186N) mutation found in melanoma mimics SEC23B phosphorylated on Ser186 similarly to what observed for SEC23B(S186D).
evidence: Multiple experiments showing similar properties between S186N and S186D mutants

claim: SEC23B(S186N) does not bind efficiently FBXW5, SEC24C, and SEC24D
source: In fact, SEC23B(S186N) does not bind efficiently FBXW5, SEC24C, and SEC24D, and promotes autophagy, in agreement with a possible advantageous role resulting from increasing autophagic flux to ensure tumour cell homeostasis (Rybstein et al., 2018).
evidence: Binding experiments showing reduced interactions

claim: SEC23B(S186N) promotes autophagy
source: In fact, SEC23B(S186N) does not bind efficiently FBXW5, SEC24C, and SEC24D, and promotes autophagy, in agreement with a possible advantageous role resulting from increasing autophagic flux to ensure tumour cell homeostasis (Rybstein et al., 2018).
evidence: LC3 puncta and flux measurements showing increased autophagy

claim: FBXW5 targets SEC23B for degradation to limit autophagy during basal, unperturbed conditions
source: In this study, we demonstrated that FBXW5 targets SEC23B for degradation to limit autophagy during basal, unperturbed conditions.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing FBXW5-mediated degradation and autophagy regulation

claim: Upon induction of autophagy by nutrient deprivation, ULK1 phosphorylates Ser186 in SEC23B, inhibiting its interaction with and degradation via FBXW5
source: Upon induction of autophagy by nutrient deprivation, ULK1 phosphorylates Ser186 in SEC23B, inhibiting its interaction with and degradation via FBXW5.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing starvation-induced phosphorylation and stabilization

claim: The resulting increased levels of SEC23B are crucial for proper autophagic flux
source: The resulting increased levels of SEC23B are crucial for proper autophagic flux.
evidence: Knockdown and overexpression experiments showing SEC23B requirement for autophagy

claim: Phosphorylation of Ser186 in SEC23B inhibits its binding to SEC24C and SEC24D, but not SEC24A and SEC24B
source: We also found that phosphorylation of Ser186 in SEC23B inhibits its binding to SEC24C and SEC24D, but not SEC24A and SEC24B.
evidence: Co-immunoprecipitation experiments showing differential binding

claim: Depletion of SEC24A and SEC24B, but not SEC24C and SEC24D, rescues the increase in autophagy during non-stressed conditions induced by FBXW5 silencing
source: Accordingly, depletion of SEC24A and SEC24B, but not SEC24C and SEC24D rescue the phenotype (i.e., the increase in autophagy during non-stressed conditions) induced by FBXW5 silencing.
evidence: Double knockdown experiments showing paralog-specific epistasis

claim: The phosphorylation of Ser186 may explain the reduced secretion observed upon nutrient starvation
source: The fact that the phosphorylation of Ser186 inhibits the binding of SEC23B to SEC24C and SEC24D may explain, at least in part, the reduced secretion observed upon nutrient starvation.
evidence: Secretion assays and binding experiments showing correlation

claim: Autophagic COPII vesicles are generated from the ERGIC rather than the ERES
source: It has been suggested that autophagic COPII vesicles can be distinguished from trafficking COPII vesicles by their different site of generation, that is autophagic COPII vesicles are generated from the ERGIC rather than the ERES, and they are potent stimulators of LC3 lipidation in response to starvation (Ge et al., 2015; Ge et al., 2014).
evidence: Citation to published literature on autophagic COPII vesicles

claim: Autophagic COPII vesicles are potent stimulators of LC3 lipidation in response to starvation
source: It has been suggested that autophagic COPII vesicles can be distinguished from trafficking COPII vesicles by their different site of generation, that is autophagic COPII vesicles are generated from the ERGIC rather than the ERES, and they are potent stimulators of LC3 lipidation in response to starvation (Ge et al., 2015; Ge et al., 2014).
evidence: Citation to published literature on LC3 lipidation

claim: PI3KC3, which is activated by ULK1, is required for the relocation of COPII components to the ERGIC
source: PI3KC3, which is activated by ULK1, is required for the relocation of COPII components to the ERGIC (Ge et al., 2015; Ge et al., 2014).
evidence: Citation to published literature on PI3KC3 function

claim: At least a subpopulation of autophagic COPII vesicles present at the ERGIC upon starvation contain SEC23B phosphorylated on Ser186 by ULK1
source: Our results indicate that at least a subpopulation of autophagic COPII vesicles present at the ERGIC upon starvation contain SEC23B phosphorylated on Ser186 by ULK1.
evidence: Localization and phosphorylation experiments showing ERGIC-localized phospho-SEC23B

claim: In yeast, phosphorylation of Sec24 by casein kinase one promotes its binding to autophagy factors to increase autophagosome abundance
source: Interestingly, in yeast, phosphorylation of Sec24 by casein kinase one promotes its binding to autophagy factors to increase autophagosome abundance (Davis et al., 2016), which is reminiscent of what we found in human cells (i.e., phosphorylation of SEC23B by ULK1 induces the localization of SEC23B and, consequently, SEC24A and SEC24B to the ERGIC to promote the autophagic flux).
evidence: Citation to published yeast study showing evolutionary conservation

claim: In the presence of nutrients, the basal activity of ULK1 mediates the phosphorylation of SEC16A, promoting the assembly of COPII complexes at the ERES
source: Recently, it has been shown that, in presence of nutrients, the basal activity of ULK1 mediates the phosphorylation of SEC16A (promoting the assembly of COPII complexes at the ERES) and that, in response to starvation, the activation of ULK1 induces the dissociation of SEC23A from SEC31A (inhibiting the secretory pathway) (Joo et al., 2016; Gan et al., 2017).
evidence: Citation to published studies on ULK1 regulation of COPII

claim: In response to starvation, the activation of ULK1 induces the dissociation of SEC23A from SEC31A, inhibiting the secretory pathway
source: Recently, it has been shown that, in presence of nutrients, the basal activity of ULK1 mediates the phosphorylation of SEC16A (promoting the assembly of COPII complexes at the ERES) and that, in response to starvation, the activation of ULK1 induces the dissociation of SEC23A from SEC31A (inhibiting the secretory pathway) (Joo et al., 2016; Gan et al., 2017).
evidence: Citation to published studies on ULK1 regulation of secretion

claim: In the absence of nutrients, activated ULK1 promotes the phosphorylation of SEC23B on Ser186, inducing SEC23B accumulation and the formation of autophagic COPII vesicles
source: Our study shows that, in the absence of nutrients, activated ULK1 promotes the phosphorylation of SEC23B on Ser186, inducing SEC23B accumulation and the formation of autophagic COPII vesicles.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing starvation-induced phosphorylation and COPII function in autophagy

claim: The decrease in the abundance of the SEC23B-SEC24C/D complexes likely contributes to inhibit the secretory pathway
source: Moreover, the decrease in the abundance of the SEC23B-SEC24C/D complexes likely contributes to inhibit the secretory pathway.
evidence: Binding experiments and secretion assays showing correlation

claim: ULK1 functions as a switch necessary to commit COPII to autophagy in response to starvation
source: Altogether, our results provide evidence for one of the molecular mechanisms by which ULK1 functions as a switch necessary to commit COPII to autophagy in response to starvation.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing ULK1-dependent regulation of COPII function in autophagy

claim: In the presence of nutrients, FBXW5 limits COPII-mediated autophagosome biogenesis
source: We propose that, in the presence of nutrients, FBXW5 limits COPII-mediated autophagosome biogenesis.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing FBXW5 limits basal autophagy through SEC23B degradation

claim: Inhibition of FBXW5-mediated SEC23B degradation by ULK1 ensures efficient execution of the autophagic cascade in response to nutrient starvation
source: Inhibition of this event by ULK1 ensures efficient execution of the autophagic cascade in response to nutrient starvation.
evidence: Multiple experiments showing ULK1 blocks FBXW5 function to promote autophagy
